item.title: Report: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling to miss at least a month with an ankle injury
item.description: The 49ers lost wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling to an ankle injury on their way to a win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia on Thursday and it will reportedly be a bit of time before the rookie is able to return to action.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers lost wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling to an ankle injury on their way to a win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia on Thursday and it will reportedly be a bit of time before the rookie is able to return to action.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Stribling is expected to be out for at least a month. Stribling is reportedly dealing with a deltoid sprain and is still consulting doctors about his options, but is not currently expected to need surgery.

The time frame makes Stribling a candidate for injured reserve.

Stribling was the first pick of the second round in this year's draft. He started against the Rams and played 21 snaps before leaving the game with his injury.

Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and Demarcus Robinson are the top three wideouts for the Niners with Stribling out of action. All three of them caught touchdowns from Brock Purdy in Thursday's win.

item.description: Welcome to the first NFL Sunday of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Week 1 of the 2026 season, where the dreams of fans that their team may be the one to hoist the Lombardi in Super Bowl LXI remain alive and well … for now.

There are plenty of storylines to keep your eyes on throughout the afternoon slate, but perhaps no team has quite as much to watch as the Pittsburgh Steelers, who have a new head coach in Mike McCarthy after Mike Tomlin stepped down this offseason. That puts McCarthy in place to reunite with four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers — the very head coach-QB duo that defeated the Steelers in Super Bowl XL.

On the other side of the ball, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is unlikely to play in Week 1, ramping up from a back injury in the offseason while also in the middle of a contract dispute with the team.

Among the key injuries to watch heading into Sunday afternoon: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle), WR Emeka Egbuka (toe) and WR Ja’Marr Chase (knee) all look poised to play in their respective openers. Meanwhile, fantasy managers got an unfortunate update on Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers, who will miss “a game or two” to start the season after undergoing a knee procedure last week.

item.title: Steelers' Joey Porter Jr. reportedly unlikely to play Sunday amid back injury, contract dispute
item.description: Joey Porter Jr. reportedly won't play vs. the Falcons on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is reportedly "unlikely" to play against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday as he deals with a back injury, according to multiple reports. Porter entered the weekend questionable with the injury.

Porter missed essentially all of training camp due to the issue. While Porter was activated from the physically unable to perform list Sept. 1 and has practiced, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy classifed Porter’s work as a “ramp-up” after the cornerback missed so much time.

Despite getting in work during practice, Porter is not expected to go in Week 1. The injury, however, might not have anything to do with his situation. Porter has been seeking a new contract all summer, and talks have not resulted in a deal just yet.

Porter spoke openly about the issue the day he was activated, saying he wasn’t sure if he would play in Week 1 if his contract situation was unresolved.

A week later, New England Patriots’ star cornerback Christian Gonzalez agreed to a massive four-year, $135 million extension with the team. That contract was expected to set the market for Porter, giving him a baseline for his next deal.

Despite that figure being out there, the Steelers and Porter still haven’t agreed to a new contract.

While the Steelers have yet to confirm Porter’s status for their Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons, the team dropped a significant hint Saturday that Porter would not play, elevating cornerback Doneiko Slaughter from the practice squad to the active roster.

It’s unclear where Porter and the Steelers go from here. The team is reportedly open to trading the star cornerback, but is hoping to receive a first-round pick in a deal, per ESPN’s Brooke Pryor. That cost has scared off potential trade partner and no serious trade discussions have taken place just yet.

Porter has established himself as a strong player after being selected by the Steelers in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. While he has yet to make the Pro Bowl in his first three NFL seasons, he’s graded out well in Pro Football Focus’ metrics.

The Steelers will undoubtedly miss Porter against the Falcons on Sunday. But unless the team’s defense drastically falls apart without Porter, both sides could be looking at an extended absence for the time being.

item.title: 2026 NFL season preview, betting, odds: 1 bet I like for every NFC team
item.description: Matt Russell gives a wager he likes for all 16 NFC teams heading into the upcoming season.
item.content:encoded:
In Part 1 of our 32 bets for 32 teams ahead of the NFL season, we went up and down the AFC, looking for value in both the team futures and the player prop market; contemplating the statistical ceiling for some, and breaking down why others might not meet expectations. 

For Part 2, our attention turns to the NFC. Here is my favorite bet for all 16 teams:

Arizona Cardinals

Last season, we could feel positive statistical regression coming for Trey McBride touchdowns, as he was lined at 4.5 after a 2024 season where he scored just twice on 111 receptions. 

McBride scored 11 times. 

The market's done a better job adjusting to McBride than NFL defenses have, lining him at 6.5 touchdowns this season, but the Cardinals do have more red zone options this season. As a model of consistency with between five and 12 receptions in all but one game in 2025, and wanting to have a piece of McBride in some way, we'll bet on him to hit 100 receptions for a third straight season. 

Bet: Trey McBride over 97.5 receptions (-115, DraftKings)

Atlanta Falcons 

The Falcons took a big swing drafting Michael Penix Jr. in 2024, but it took less than two seasons for the concern over that move to come to fruition. Not only was he not a ready-made product as an older rookie, but his third torn ACL was the unfortunate answer to the questions about his durability. As a result, the Falcons signed Tua Tagovailoa on the cheap, hoping that one of them will have a career renaissance this season, but Kevin Stefanski brought Tommy Rees with him as offensive coordinator, and he has no track record for reclamation projects.

Defensively, the plan was that two first-round pass-rushers picked in 2025 would cause havoc for opponents who then had to throw into a secondary with A.J. Terrell and Jessie Bates. Jalon Walker tore his ACL in training camp, and James Pearce Jr. was suspended for the first half of the season. 

The Falcons are lined at 7.5 because there are game-breakers in place on both sides of the ball, but the players needed to put them in the best place to break games aren't there. 

Bet: Falcons under 7.5 wins (-140, DraftKings)

Carolina Panthers 

It's weird to say that the starting quarterback and the 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year need to find a better connection, but Tetairoa McMillan caught only 57.3% of the passes thrown to him last season and went without a touchdown in nine of his first 10 games. Plus, that catch percentage actually went down in the final seven games of the season, a span where McMillan had five of his seven TDs. 

If Bryce Young and McMillan find a better connection in their second season together, that should translate to at least the same number of touchdowns for someone who profiles as the prototypical red zone target. 

Bet: Tetairoa McMillan over 6.5 TDs (-105, DraftKings)

Chicago Bears 

We'll mini-spoil one of THE WINDOW's cornerstone preseason betting articles, with a long-shot play on who might lead the NFL in receiving touchdowns — a category notorious for having surprise contenders. 

McBride made a run at catching the most touchdowns from the tight end position, tying for second in the league with 11. Colston Loveland could do the same this season. 

As a rookie, Loveland racked up the targets (48) in the Bears' final four games last season, and actually tied Rome Odunze and DJ Moore for the team receiving TD lead. With Moore gone, and both Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson talking a big game about Chicago's offense this season, this is a worthy look at a massive long shot. 

Bet: Colston Loveland most receiving touchdowns in the NFL (60-1, DraftKings)

Dallas Cowboys

If this happens, it will probably be insufferable — but, should a defensive overhaul work, featuring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker coming over from the Eagles, there's more than a non-zero chance that the Cowboys have a really good season. 

We already know that Dak Prescott's numbers will be there, so there's no need to sell anyone on whether he'd be the lead Cowboys' candidate for MVP, that is, if Dallas does win 12-plus games, the NFC East, and earns at least a top-two seed in the NFC. 

Classic Cowboys media attention will drive Prescott's candidacy past the top six choices on the oddsboard, all of whom come from the AFC. 

Bet: Dak Prescott to win MVP (12-1)

Detroit Lions

We had an under for a star quarterback in our AFC article, based on the double-premise of: A team being in more positive game-states than last season, while also expressing concern about injuries depressing their counting stats this season. 

In the NFC, the "pro" case for a Lions bounce-back season is how soft Detroit's schedule is, and if being the lookahead-line favorite in 14 of their first 15 games (and often by more than a touchdown) translates to fourth-quarter leads, Jared Goff will be in less shootouts this season. 

On the negative side, the Lions' offensive line is a far cry from when it was one of the best units in the NFL, buying time for Goff to find receivers down the field during his four straight seasons of 4,400-plus passing yards, and keeping him upright well enough not to miss a game.

Bet: Jared Goff under 4,099.5 passing yards (-110, Bet365)

Green Bay Packers

The Packers didn't fire Matt LaFleur, which, for a few days, seemed very much in play after another unceremonious postseason exit. 

Green Bay might be thrilled with an opportunity to blow a lead in the playoffs this season. 

Micah Parsons will miss at least the first four games as part of his return from an ACL tear, which compromises a defense that's invested in him being the centerpiece. 

Offensively, a great first season from Jordan Love set expectations that haven't been met since. A once-deep skill-position group has thinned out with wide receiver departures, Josh Jacobs' off-field issues and Tucker Kraft dealing with his own ACL rehab. 

In a tough division, and LaFleur potentially on his last chance, getting plus-money on the Packers to miss the playoffs is the way to fade Green Bay. 

Bet: Packers to miss the playoffs (+122, DraftKings)

Minnesota Vikings

In 2024, Sam Darnold was getting so much support in the media for Comeback Player of the Year, voters had to be reminded that the award is not supposed to go to players who come back from merely being bad. 

Kyler Murray was ostensibly hurt last season, which creates just enough plausible deniability for if he ends up being an equally good fit as Darnold was in Kevin O'Connell's offense (4,319 yards, 35 TDs).

Plus, Murray has never thrown for 4,000 yards or 30-plus touchdowns, so if he can replicate Darnold's season on a Vikings team that had nine wins with awful quarterback play last season, Murray will be the Comeback Player of the Year. 

Bet: Kyler Murray to win Comeback Player of the Year (+600, DraftKings)

Los Angeles Rams

It's not often a No. 2 running back is widely available in the season-long prop markets, but the line between Kyren Williams and Blake Corum is starting to blur. In 2024, when Corum was a rookie, he merely spelled Williams, getting out-carried 316 to 58 (and it was only that close because Williams missed a game).

Last season, though, the split tightened, to 259-145 (64.1% to 35.9%) — and even more in the final 11 games (164-116, or 58.5% to 41.5%). 

For the season, Williams had just three carries that went for more than 20 yards. Corum had five after the Rams Week 8 bye, along with five of his six touchdowns, on the way to a higher yards-per-carry average for the season. 

Corum's one minor injury to Williams away from having the carry split tilted his way for the season, and between his explosiveness and the Rams' penchant for handing it off at the goal line, Corum scoring more than 10 touchdowns isn't out of the question.

Bet: Blake Corum: 10-plus TDs (+500, DraftKings)

New Orleans Saints

The longest shot of the year is reliant on the ball-knowers on the Protector of the Year panel, made up of former offensive linemen. 

It might be a chicken-and-egg thing, but if Kellen Moore and Tyler Shough can take the Saints up a notch from 238.4 passing yards per game and 10 touchdowns in 10 starts, that could either bring attention to the rest of the offense — including the line, or maybe good O-line play would be the reason for a possible leap? Especially since Shough was sacked 31 times in his 10 games last season. 

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Either way, Erik McCoy returns after missing most of 2025, but, before getting hurt, he had the best pass-blocking grade among all centers, according to PFF. And that was one season after having the best overall grade in 2024, and ranking fifth in 2023. 

It's the longest shot of our 32 bets, but McCoy's been good enough for long enough that he could be the recognized MVP on an improved offense.

Bet: Erik McCoy to win Protector of the Year (175-1, Bet365)

New York Giants 

The Giants would love Jaxson Dart to go against his admirable instincts and get down, or out of bounds, when he scrambles, but we'd be remiss not to note that he's more of an injury candidate than most others at his position. That's why the Giants have Jameis Winston, just in case. 

Even when healthy, Dart averaged just 189.3 passing yards per game in his rookie season. If he managed to play all 17 games this season, that would just barely crawl over his yardage total. 

With the hope for Malik Nabers to be running at full speed early, the assumption that the New York's offense is going to take off with John Harbaugh as head coach and Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator this season seems overly optimistic.

If Dart misses so much as one game, he'll need to average 200 passing yards in the other 16 games, and a 15-game season would require 210 YPG. That's more than Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Aaron Rodgers, Bryce Young, Cam Ward and several other veteran quarterbacks managed last season. 

Bet: Jaxson Dart under 3,150.5 passing yards (-115, DraftKings)

Philadelphia Eagles

Given his talent level and the defense he plays on, if Jalen Carter is never at least in contention for Defensive Player of the Year, we're going to feel like Ben Affleck's character, at the construction site, telling Matt Damon's Will Hunting what a waste it would be if he never fullfils the promise of his God-given ability, 

The favorite, Myles Garrett, is now with the Rams, which actually hurts his candidacy, as voters may be less likely to reward the result of an obviously stacked defensive line, making this award category more wide open than many think.

Bet: Jalen Carter to win Defensive Player of the Year (25-1)

San Francisco 49ers

As part of the 49ers' efforts to bleed as much as they can out of the end of their once-great core's careers, they added the once-great Mike Evans to a receiving corps that has the betting market expecting something from the long-time Buccaneer. 

I'm expecting relatively little. 

With 11 straight seasons of at laest 1,000 receiving yards to start his career, Evans was once reliable to hit that milestone. If that's why he's lined into the 800s after a season where he played eight games and had 368 yards, then that's an opportunity to fade a future Hall-of-Famer who's further down the road than any of the Niners one might worry about getting hurt this season, and already suffering from a soft tissue (groin) injury. 

Bet: Mike Evans under 824.5 receiving yards (-110, DraftKings)

Seattle Seahawks 

It's the NFC version of a Defensive Player of the Year long-shot bet we made in the AFC edition, as we look at another dominant cornerback on a highly regarded defense. 

Devon Witherspoon is used in a variety of ways by the Seahawks, adding a Super Bowl sack to his résumé as a top cover-corner and one of the best tacklers at the position as well. 

Seattle was a surprise contender through much of last season, but with voters ready to respect its defense this season, and the sheer number of pass-rushers splitting the impact of the defensive front, if the ball finds Witherspoon for a couple of extra splash plays, he'll get attention for DPOY. 

Bet: Devon Witherspoon to win Defensive Player of the Year (+5500, FanDuel)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers

As an exercise, draw a line on the oddsboard where you think the cut off is for teams that are capable of winning the NFC. Last season, you likely would have drawn that line north of the Seahawks. 

This year, you can hit the 10th choice and still just be getting to a favorite for a division, which means the market is not just down on Tampa Bay, but it doesn't think much of the other three teams in the NFC South.

Baker Mayfield, a healthier skill-position group with better defined roles and a top-tier offensive line can take advantage of the other three teams in the division, on the way to stretching last season's 8-2 start to something similar over 17 games — especially if Todd Bowles' defensive youth movement works better than expected. 

A high playoff seed is just as possible as what Seattle accomplished last season, making it worth the long-shot price on a team with as good a path as any to the Super Bowl.

Bet: Buccaneers to win NFC (22-1, DraftKings)

Washington Commanders

Simply put, now that Laremy Tunsil is out for an extended period of time, the Commanders offensive line isn't going to be able to protect Jayden Daniels, and there's no reason to believe last year's poor defense will be transformed by the addition of Sonny Styles, a rookie inside linebacker. 

Against a schedule that is more difficult than it appears at first blush, getting to a Week 11 Monday-nighter at home against the Bengals at 4-5 would be an accomplishment. Even then, Washington would need to split its final eight games, which include Houston, at Minnesota, at Jacksonville, and at Dallas, after that prime-time tilt with Cincinnati.

Bet: Commanders under 7.5 wins (-125, DraftKings)

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL season kicks off with a slew of intriguing matchups, and within those matchups lies a slew of intriguing NFL betting trends.

For instance, did you know that the Los Angeles Rams have covered the point spread in more than 70% of their regular-season games over the past season-and-a-half? 

Or that the Buffalo Bills — a short Week 1 favorite — have been money in that role over the past four years — but have come up empty the last six times they've visited Houston (where they will play on Sunday)?

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Or that the Cincinnati Bengals have been a Week 1 bust for the past half-dozen years — as have the New York Giants for the last 15?

Well, now you do. For more interesting — and potentially actionable — NFL betting trends, check out the following report that covers five of the top games on the Week 1 docket.

Buccaneers at Bengals (-3.5, 50.5)

Kickoff: Sunday, 1 p.m. ET

Moneyline: Buccaneers +165/Bengals -200

• Cincinnati halted a three-game season-opening losing skid last season when it barely held off the Browns 17-16. However, the Bengals came up short as a 5-point road favorite, their fourth straight non-cover in Week 1.

During this decade, Cincinnati is 2-4 SU and 1-5 ATS in season openers.

• On the complete opposite end of the Week 1 NFL betting trends spectrum, the Buccaneers have won five consecutive season openers (4-1 ATS).

During this stretch, Tampa Bay is 3-0 SU and ATS as a visitor.

• The under is 6-1 in Bengals season openers since 2019, with the last four in a row staying low. Total combined points in those seven contests: 44, 29, 51 (overtime), 43 (overtime), 27, 26 and 31.

This particular NFL betting trend can be pinned on Cincinnati's offense, which has averaged just 15.7 points in season openers — even though quarterback Joe Burrow started the last six of them.

Meanwhile, the under also has cashed in three of Tampa Bay's last four Week 1 outings, with only one contest hurdling 43 points.

• According to SportsOddsHistory.com, only seven Week 1 games since 2022 have closed with a total of 50 points or higher. The under is 5-2 in those contests.

Bills (-1.5, 44.5) at Texans

Kickoff: Sunday, 1 p.m. ET

Moneyline: Bills -115/Texans -105

• Despite going 12-5 last season — its seventh straight double-digit win campaign — Buffalo finished underwater for bettors, going 8-9 ATS.

On the bright side of the NFL betting trend ledger, though, the Bills have delivered big-time profits as a short favorite in recent years. Since 2022, they are 11-2 SU and 10-2-1 ATS when laying three points or fewer (including 8-1 SU and 7-1-1 ATS on the road).

• Houston kicked off the 2025 campaign in Los Angeles with a 14-9 loss to the Rams as a 3-point underdog. With that, the franchise fell to 3-7-1 SU and 4-7 ATS in its last 11 Week 1 contests.

But the Texans won nine straight games to close the 2025 regular season, including four straight outright upsets as an underdog.

• Houston has owned the Bills lately, going 7-2 SU and 6-3 ATS dating to 2009. This includes six consecutive victories at home (5-1 ATS).

Two of the Texans' home triumphs over Buffalo came in the last two seasons by near identical scores: 23-20 in 2024 (as a 1.5-point favorite) and 23-19 in 2025 (as a 4.5-point underdog).

Not only did the under hit in both contests, each of the last six head-to-head battles in Texas have stayed low.

Packers at Vikings (-1.5, 46.5)

Kickoff: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET

Moneyline: Packers -102/Vikings -118

• Green Bay pummeled bettors last year, complementing a solid 9-7-1 SU record by going 5-10-2 ATS.

After upsetting the Lions 31-24 as a 3-point underdog on Thanksgiving Day, the Packers closed 1-4 SU and 0-3-2 ATS. 

Even with the Turkey Day victory in Detroit, Green Bay went 2-6-1 ATS as a visitor.

• Minnesota followed a dismal 4-8 SU/ATS start to last season with a five-game winning streak. The Vikings covered the point spread in each of the first four victories before beating Green Bay 16-3 as a 13-point home favorite in the finale.

Bet the Vikings to cover the spread at sportsbooks

Minnesota also finished 3-0 at home (2-0-1 ATS) after starting 1-4 SU and ATS at U.S. Bank Stadium.

• The Packers have just one win in their last five trips to Minnesota (1-3-1 ATS), all as an underdog. In fact, the favorite 7-2 SU and 6-2-1 ATS in this rivalry since Week 18 of 2022.

Over that nine-game span, there have been seven double-digit blowouts, and the losing team has scored 10 points or fewer six times.

• Since the start of the 2024 season, 11 of Minnesota's 16 home games have come up short of the closing total — including each of the final six contests in 2025.

Cowboys (-2.5, 48.5) at NY Giants

Kickoff: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET

Moneyline: Cowboys -150/Giants +125

• Dallas finished 12-5 SU in three straight seasons from 2021-23 and produced solid profits along the way (33-18 ATS). Since then, however, the Cowboys are 14-19-1 SU and 14-20 ATS.

Dallas was favored 13 times in the past two years, going 6-7 SU and 3-10 ATS.

• Although they posted a third consecutive losing season (and eighth in the last nine), the 2025 Giants at least didn't bury their supporters. New York finished 9-8 ATS, capped by season-ending blowout wins over the Raiders (34-10) and Cowboys (34-17).

Despite that latter result, Dallas is 16-2 SU and 12-6 ATS versus New York over the past nine seasons. Also, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott is 14-3 SU and 10-7 ATS against the Giants in his career, with 31 touchdown passes and nine interceptions.

• Another negative NFL betting trend that the Giants encounter right out of the chute: They have lost 13 of 15 season openers since 2011, going 3-12 ATS.

Since 2020, New York is 1-5 SU and ATS in Week 1 — and all five were double-digit defeats by an average margin of 20.2 points. That includes a 40-0 home loss to Dallas in the 2023 opener.

• From 2020-24, the under cashed at an astonishing 60.2% clip in Giants games (56 unders, 27 overs, 1 push).

That NFL betting trend finally flipped last year, when 11 of New York's 16 contests topped the total (including six of the last seven overall and five of the last six at home).

Meanwhile, the over is 33-17-1 in Cowboys games over the past three seasons (16-8-1 at home, 17-9 on the road).

item.title: Oddsmakers rank every NFL starting QBs by point-spread value: Josh Allen is the clear No. 1
item.description: Josh Allen is the most valuable QB in the NFL by value to the point spread, according to oddsmakers.
item.content:encoded:
Playing quarterback in the NFL is the most valuable position in team sports, but every team has a different starting and backup QB, so determining the gap in point-spread value between the two can be an extremely useful tool for bettors.

Put another way: How much would the spread move if Patrick Mahomes was suddenly injured leading up to a game and Justin Fields was forced to be the starter?

It's an important question for bettors (and bookmakers) alike to answer, and one that has real-world applications every NFL season.

For example, back in January when Denver Broncos QB Bo Nix was ruled out of the AFC championship game with a broken ankle suddenly (leaving Jarrett Stidham as the starter), the Broncos went from a lookahead line of Denver -1.5 to +4.5 against the New England Patriots (which was then quickly bet up to Denver +5.5).

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Readers of last year's version of this article would have known that was an overcorrection and could have placed a wager on the Broncos to cover, as oddsmakers had pegged Nix as worth 3.85 points more against the spread than Stidham before the season began. The market ended up moving back towards Denver and the Broncos closed as 3.5-point underdogs (a 4-point difference from the lookahead line). Denver lost 10-7, but covered the number.

When moving a line based off a QB change, there are a wide variety of factors oddsmakers consider, including:

  • The current line and how close it is to a key number

  • Starting QB's talent level, plus the quality of the backup

  • How much of the offense would need to change with the backup

  • Strength of the play caller and head coach

  • Overall talent level of the team (how good is rest of offense and defense)

  • Where/when the game is being played

Over the summer, I polled 11 oddsmakers from 10 different legal sportsbooks and prediction markets across the country, and asked them for the difference in point spread if the starting QB and backup (both healthy) were playing at home against a league-average team. I then took all 11 different ATS values, averaged them together and ranked the starting QBs in order from greatest impact to least. Oddsmakers were granted anonymity to honestly voice their opinions of QBs they were higher or lower on than consensus.

Last year, Josh Allen moved into the No. 1 overall spot for the first time, slightly ahead of Patrick Mahomes; this year, Allen has put some distance between the two QBs. After an MVP season (and with rookie Ty Simpson as his backup), Los Angeles Rams QB Matthew Stafford has catapulted up to No. 3 overall. Stafford is followed by Drake Maye and Lamar Jackson.

In one of the more surprising moves, Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow moved from fifth last year (5.60 points ATS) to 12th this year (4.89). There was certainly some disagreement among oddsmakers over the ATS difference between Burrow and his new backup Joe Flacco, as six oddsmakers had that difference as 4.5 points or less and four had it as 5.75 points or greater.

Here is how much every starting QB is worth relative to his backup, according to the 11-oddsmaker panel:

Top 5 QBs by ATS value

1. Josh Allen, Bills (7.23 points ATS)

Backup QB: Kyle Allen

The good news for Bills fans is that there now isn't any debate among oddsmakers about which QB is the most valuable player against the spread compared to his backup — it's Allen's world. The bad news is that another heartbreaking playoff defeat left Allen's Bills short of the Super Bowl — again.

"To me, he's the most talented QB in the league," one oddsmaker told me. "The durability as well would put him ahead of Mahomes."

To that point, Allen hasn't missed a game since his rookie season, and at 6-foot-5, 237 pounds he is able to punish defensive backs, safeties and even linebackers when he chooses to run the ball. Allen has at least 421 rushing yards in every season of his career and scored 14 rushing TDs (along with 3,668 yards and 25 TDs passing) this past season.

As one oddsmaker put it: "He is the entire Bills identity right now."

Not one, but two oddsmakers had Allen worth nine points more to the spread than his new backup Kyle Allen and Josh Allen was the only QB that all 11 oddsmakers had as worth at least worth six points against the number.

Still, concerns about turnovers remain and for Allen (10 INTs, 6 fumbles last season) they reared their ugly head in a very winnable postseason loss to the Broncos in which he was responsible for four turnovers.

The Bills have won at least 11 games for six consecutive seasons and Allen (+650) is the favorite to win MVP. Buffalo's over/under for this season is 10.5 and the Bills should be in the postseason again (-350 to make the playoffs).

Is this finally the year for the Bills and the NFL's most valuable QB against the spread?

2. Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs (6.32 points ATS)

Backup QB: Justin Fields

There's no shame in being No. 2, but it isn't a familiar position for the three-time Super Bowl-winning QB Mahomes. Coming off a disappointing season where he cleared 300 yards passing just twice (and tossed 11 INTs), the Chiefs went 6-11 and Mahomes tore both his ACL and MCL in Week 15, there are a few more questions regarding the three-time MVP from pundits. Oddsmakers aren't as concerned.

"You could see when he was off the field last year how big a swing it was for the Chiefs," one Vegas oddsmaker told Yahoo Sports. "He is a man amongst boys when it comes to quarterbacks. This is a pivotal season for him."

Mahomes was fully cleared for training camp participation coming off his knee injuries, but even if he indeed starts Week 1 it's unlikely he's back to his full powers right away. Mahomes was third last year in clutch-weighted expected points added through rushes (24.7), and his running has always been a little under appreciated. It's an element of his game that Mahomes has admitted he'll have to use a little less, especially early on in his recovery.

Check out all of Yahoo's sports betting content here in our new betting hub

One oddsmaker noted that he'd have Mahomes around 3.5 points more valuable ATS to start the season and closer to six full points later in the season when Mahomes was closer to full health.

"Everything I've been reading and hearing has been very optimistic, so I fully expect Mahomes to look like the same guy we've seen," a longtime oddsmaker noted. "The interesting piece is the difference in backups with Fields and Minshew. From a rating perspective, I have them rated very similar — and maybe that's doing a disservice to Fields, but he's never lived up to the potential some people thought he had out of Ohio State. Backing up Mahomes could be the best thing ever to happen to Fields."

Mahomes has always had a weaker backup QB (Carson Wentz, Gardner Minshew, Justin Fields) than many other teams, which has boosted Mahomes' spread value, but as one oddsmaker said, "if I had to pick one [between Mahomes and Allen], it's still Mahomes."

3. Matthew Stafford, LA Rams (6.16 points ATS)

Backup QB: Ty Simpson

One of the biggest risers in this column year over year — he was tied for 16th at 4.10 points ATS last year — Stafford is here both because he had a terrific season (4,707 passing yards, 46 TDs, No. 4 in QBR, won MVP) and because his backup is rookie QB Ty Simpson out of Alabama.

"Who knows if Simpson take a snap this year, but I have him rated at zero," a long-time oddsmaker remarked. "Last year, [the backup] was Jimmy Garappolo who obviously was a proven commodity and we had good data on him. That's going to make up some of that difference year over year for Stafford, and obviously he played at an MVP level. The old man still has it."

The Super Bowl favorites at sportsbooks, Los Angeles is tied for the NFL's highest win total at 11.5 and has the best odds (-500) of any team to make the postseason. Keeping Stafford healthy — remember the preseason back concerns last year? — is of paramount importance for another postseason run.

"I might be a little lower on him just because of the Sean McVay system, and you add in the fact that the backup is a first-round pick," said one Vegas oddsmaker who is a bigger believer in Simpson. "If Stafford got hurt, I have full faith in McVay making the offense easier for Simpson. I don't expect Stafford to fall off physically — he was never a runner earlier in his career and I haven't seen any drop-off in arm strength. One thing to worry about is his durability."

Several oddsmakers did express concern about Simpson's ability to step in right away if Stafford was injured, though, and one stated that "you just don't know what you're going to get" from a rookie QB like Simpson, who also only started 15 college games in his Alabama career.

As one NFL risk manager put simply, "I know he's getting older but going from a Hall of Fame QB to an unproven rookie would be a major odds swing."

4. Drake Maye, Patriots (5.93 points ATS)

Backup QB: Tommy DeVito

There's no doubt that Maye wishes he could've played better in New England's postseason run to Super Bowl 60. There's also no doubt that the 2025 MVP runner-up had a terrific sophomore campaign and now is one of the most valuable QBs against the spread in the league. And there's no doubt that having DeVito as his backup helps to boost Maye's spread value.

"Obviously, Maye is ascending," one veteran Vegas bookmaker mentioned over the phone. "DeVito in my opinion is one of the worst backups on this list, though. I think he was a great story [with the Giants], but I don't think too much of him."

When I did this exercise entering Maye's rookie year, oddsmakers had him as 1.6 points ATS worse than Patriots starter Jacoby Brissett. Maye was 23rd last season, rated 3.08 points ATS better than Josh Dobbs. A season where he led New England to a 14-3 record and an AFC East division title, along with topping the NFL in Total QBR (77.1) and Total Expected Points Added (169.96) has resulted in another jump for the Patriots' franchise QB.

There was a little wider range for Maye, with oddsmakers valuing him anywhere from 4 points to 7.5 points of spread value compared to DeVito.

The oddsmaker who was lowest on Maye, cautioned, "I did move Maye up slightly from last year. While there's a definite downgrade to DeVito, I exercise a little caution on not going too out there on Maye, as you could see some regression with him and certainly the Patriots have a much more difficult schedule as well."

5. Lamar Jackson, Ravens (5.89 points ATS)

Backup QB: Tyler Huntley

A staple of the top five of these rankings over the past three seasons, Jackson has been third, third and now fifth — just behind Maye. Despite an injury-plagued season, oddsmakers don't have too many fears about Jackson slowing down — as seen by Baltimore's win total (11.5, tied with Rams for NFL's highest) and Jackson (+850) owning the second-best MVP odds.

"No concerns whatsoever with Lamar," an East Coast oddsmaker told Yahoo Sports. "This year-over-year was a difference between Tyler Huntley and Cooper Rush. That's why for me the ATS difference shrunk was because of the backup."

Huntley has shown he's a capable backup for small stretches, and that the offense doesn't have to change too much if he's inserted as the starter. Yes, a new head coach in Jesse Minter and a new offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle will require an adjustment period, but Jackson was still ninth in QBR (62.9) and 18th in EPA/play (0.07) in a down year.

"He was injured for half of the season and the Ravens had an off year in general," one Vegas bookmaker explained. "Lamar still has his running ability and evasiveness. Not the greatest passer, but he was forced to work on that last year. This year, with a new system, we have high expectations that he'll throw more effectively. He'll still be a really big problem and threat to the defense."

Full rankings

Biggest riser

Malik Willis, Dolphins (+7.87 points ATS)

Backup QB: Quinn Ewers

Willis was a multi-year backup with the Green Bay Packers behind Jordan Love, and entered last season as 4.73 points ATS worse than Love. He signed a three-year, $67.5 million contract with the Miami Dolphins in free agency and enters this season 3.14 points ATS more valuable than backup QB Quinn Ewers.

Willis will have a steep task as Miami's starting QB in the beginning of a rebuild, but he does have an opportunity he wouldn't have gotten in Green Bay. Can De'Von Achane catch passes, too?

Biggest fallers

J.J. McCarthy, Vikings (-5.07 points ATS)

Starting QB: Kyler Murray

The former Michigan Wolverine and 2024 No. 10 overall pick has had a rough go of it in the NFL thus far, losing his rookie season to injury and struggling mightily (11 TDs, 12 INTs, under 182 yards passing in eight of 10 starts, 57.6% completion percentage).

One Vegas oddsmaker: "I didn't see McCathy as being another Tom Brady coming out of Michigan, but it was tough to watch some of those throws. Kyler's stock has gone down as well, but you can't go with McCarthy after what we saw last year."

McCarthy was the presumed starter last year in Minnesota and oddsmakers had him as 2.02 points ATS better than Sam Howell; now, he's rated 3.05 points ATS worse than free-agent signee Kyler Murray.

"I'm not completely out on McCarthy, but I understand why they made the move," an oddsmaker revealed. Murray was the No. 1 overall pick for a reason. Kyler got to pick his team and he saw the Vikings as the best situation."

Minnesota's starting QB battle was recently decided, with the Vikings naming Murray as the starter.

Tua Tagovailoa, Dolphins (-3.48 points ATS)

Backup QB: Michael Penix Jr.

Released by Miami back in March, Tagovailoa will cost the Dolphins a league-record $99.2 million in dead money against the salary cap over the next two seasons. Tua was injured again last season, but when was on the field he also tossed a career-high 15 INTs (and only 20 TDs) and had a career-low 43 rushing yards. He also was 26th in QBR (37.5).

He'll be battling Michael Penix Jr. (also coming off an injury) for the starting job. Oddsmakers don't have high hopes for a turnaround.

"I think Tua is going to end up the starter there personally, but it's hard to differentiate between those two QBs," one oddsmaker observed.

To wit: Penix Jr. averaged 0.02 EPA/play last season (24th) and Tagovailoa averaged 0.0 EPA/play (28th).

It's a precipitous drop for the former No. 5 overall pick, who was worth 4.48 points ATS in 2024 and 4.50 points ATS in 2025. Now, he's last in the league in the eyes of oddsmakers, worth just 1.02 points more than Penix Jr.

Quick-hitters from oddsmakers on some other notable QBs

  1. Justin Herbert, LA Chargers (5.65 points ATS)

  • "There's been almost no talk of him this offseason. Everyone knows he's almost in that elite status, just doesn't have the accolades to back it up. [Mike] McDaniel coming in should help. [Jim] Harbaugh is the CEO, so McDaniels can run the offense. I think Herbert is going be the biggest winner of that scenario. Trey Lance really hasn't shown anything."

T-8. Jalen Hurts, Eagles (5.25)

  • "I did downgrade Hurts half a point from the start of last year. I think some of this is predicated on Tanner McKee. For whatever reason, Eagles fans love McKee. Hurts has a new offensive coordinator coming in, and I think it's an upgrade. He may be under center more. I think Hurts has a bounce-back year and he's still dangerous with his legs. Certainly a dual threat and with the drop-off with him and McKee, it's one of the biggest differences in the league still. I only have three guys higher and a handful around the same."

  1. Joe Burrow, Bengals (4.89)

  • "Almost feels insulting to Burrow for him to not be higher, but this is more off of Joe Flacco last year looked like he still had some in the tank and was a solid enough game manager."

  • "I can speak from being old – Flacco is old. He's been around a long time. He can come in for an injured Burrow and finish a game. I'm not even sure that's who the Bengals want as a backup QB, but that's who he has. There's a big difference between these two guys."

  1. Caleb Williams, Bears (4.84)

  • "I did bump Caleb year over year. A lot of people in media want to talk about the highlight-reel plays, but that's not what you make a power rating out of. Did he benefit from coaching last year? Most definitely. I'm excited to see what happens when we follow up this season, I'm hesitant to put him that much higher than his backup."

  • "There's been a love affair with the Bears this offseason and how Caleb is working within this Ben Johnson system. He has the ability to make plays happen, like Mahomes, under pressure he can make quick decisions and they're usually the right ones. He struggled with his accuracy, especially early last year, which is going to drive down his market value a little bit."

  1. Sam Darnold, Seahawks (4.59)

  • "Darnold had a great year. I think Lock is capable. I was even thinking that this could've been lower, but when you lead a team to a Super Bowl you get a lot of mileage out of that. They have a great defense as well. If you're asking this question a few years ago, it's a toss up."

  1. Bo Nix, Broncos (4.30)

  • "I guess we know for sure the answer to this one, lol."

  1. C.J. Stroud, Texans (4.05)

  • "How big is that spread difference? We saw when Davis Mills would be announced the starter, the spread didn't move that much – that's why I only went with 2.5. That defense takes a way a lot of problems."

  • "This is a big year for Stroud. The Texans are loaded and could easily go far. I could see him being No. 6 or something next year. Mills is a very competent backup. You don't hear about him, 'Oh, no they're going to Mills.' He's solid. The issues Stroud had led me to 3.5, along with the respect for Mills. Texans have a great defense as well, which lessens the impact."

  1. Aaron Rodgers, Steelers (3.20)

  • "I don't think he's any good anymore. Is he going to go in and have a couple of good games? Yeah. Can he get away from anyone? Not anymore."

  • "Last year, I really didn't know what we'd get out of Rodgers. I did upgrade my rating on Rodgers slightly off my preseason rating. I think Mason Rudolph is a very capable backup. I wouldn't go to 3 as the difference – that would be a little bit too much respect for where Rodgers is at this point in his career."

  • "He played alright last year. Made the throws he needed to. He's just old. He's throwing 5 yards and the guy is running 30 yards for a TD. That's why I have it so low. I don't think there's that big a difference."

item.title: Steelers, Joey Porter Jr. reach the moment of truth
item.description: The Steelers' outdated approach to contract negotiations is not aging well.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers' outdated approach to contract negotiations is not aging well.

With the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a financial standoff and the Steelers clinging to their policy of not doing new deals after the regular season begins, no deal will be done until after the season — unless the dam suddenly breaks this morning.

So will Porter play? Despite the ESPN report that it's "unlikely" Porter will suit up against the Falcons at 1:00 p.m. ET, some within the organization still believe he'll blink. Regardless of a contract that pays less than $4 million in 2026, Porter is in a contract year. His best play could be to play and to play well, setting the stage for a shot at the open market in 2027 or, worst-case scenario, the franchise tag. (The fact that the tag at the cornerback position lags behind the top pay at the position makes that outcome even less appealing.)

The alternative is to sit, citing a back problem. It's what Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons likely planned to do in 2025, absent a new contract. Once the Cowboys realized he was committed to not playing, they traded him.

The latest ESPN report explains that the Steelers are open to listening to offers for Porter. Which is a delicate way of acknowledging that, as we've heard multiple times, no one has called.

This isn't some sudden realization that Porter could be available. He conducted a hold-in throughout training camp and the preseason. If anyone was interested in trading for Porter, they would have called by now.

The problem is that the new team would have to give the Steelers what they want for Porter, and to pay him what he's seeking. The absence of offers to date says plenty about the willingness of other teams to do that.

Which brings us back to Porter's primary options: Play for $3.924 million and hope to unlock a much better deal in 2027, or launch a Le'Veon Bell-style strategy (but with pay) — sitting out some if not most if not all games and becoming a free agent next year. (Or getting tagged.)

It's a tough spot for Porter. But there's one way to look at the glass as half-full. He was the 32nd pick in the 2023 draft, but he wasn't a first-rounder. He's not subject to the fifth-year option; for Year 5, he gets (at worst) franchise-tag money. That puts him ahead of where he would have been, if the Dolphins hadn't lost their 2023 first-round pick and if Porter had been the 32nd name off the board.

Regardless, Porter has to decide whether to take a stand by sitting out, or to grab his helmet and play. It's a decision that only Porter can make, and he needs to make it within the next couple of hours.

item.title: NFL survivor contest picks, predictions, advice, strategy: My favorite Week 1 selections
item.description: NFL survivor pools are back and Matt Russell runs through Week 1, giving his favorite picks to help you advance.
item.content:encoded:
You've got a better chance of stepping up into the hole against Derrick Henry than you do of stopping the momentum of NFL Survivor contests in the current football betting landscape. 

The world's largest (legal) contest, hosted at Circa Sports in Las Vegas, has over 20,000 entries for its guaranteed $20 million pool, and it's not even the biggest prize available in the space for this coming season.

The siren's song of "just" needing to pick one winner per week in America's most dissected sport makes everyone believe they can navigate the perils and potholes that the unpredictability of football supplies, but there's more to it than just "pick and pray."

Upgrade to Fantasy Plus and gain your edge in player projections and much more

Of course, you don't need to play in a high-roller edition of survivor. You, your friends, and family can play along as well here at Yahoo Sports, but a smaller pool of participants also changes the calculus when it comes to strategy. After all, the fewer the entrants, the less conceptual risk is necessary. 

Each week (until we've exhausted all reasonable paths of survival), we'll look at the Survivor Contest landscape and the best options available while understanding that it matters who you've already taken and what you might be giving up by burning a team that week. 

Week 1 moneylines

How likely is a team to win and you'll advance? The betting market provides the answer to that each week with the moneyline, which we can convert to an implied win probability.

Market power ratings

It's not as simple as picking the team most likely to win, because once you use that team, you can't use them again. What is simple is that if you're going to make it through the 18-week season, then you need to use 18 teams. That means, at some point, you'll be trusting the 18th-best team in the NFL — an unnerving thought. 

Here's a list of the current top 18 teams (with help from the betting market), and an estimation of their value to the point spread: 

  • Rams: 19.7

  • Seahawks: 18.1

  • Bills: 17.8

  • Ravens: 17.3

  • Lions: 16.7

  • Chargers: 16.7

  • Chiefs: 16.5

  • Packers: 16.5

  • 49ers: 16.5

  • Texans: 16.5

  • Eagles: 16.2

  • Patriots: 16.2

  • Bears: 15.9

  • Cowboys: 15.7

  • Broncos: 15.7

  • Bengals: 15.7

  • Jaguars: 14.6

  • Vikings: 14.0

Picking the most likely team to win each week, or the highest available team on this list above, means that you're giving up the opportunity to use them again later, and while every week is technically created equal, trusting a team in September is nerve-wracking, but doing so at some point in December is real tension. 

Week 1's top choices

As we look at the best options for Week 1 and onward, we'll be factoring in the decision tree that will sprout from that pick. The implied probability derived from the moneyline should answer any questions about why the favorite should win, but the nuance is found in what you're giving up by using them now and not later (with a projected point spread projection for those matchups). 

Jaguars (78.6%) over Browns 

Jacksonville's not the biggest favorite in Week 1, but you're backing a team that won nine straight games to end the regular season a year ago. 

On the other side, the Browns have tabbed Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback, but there's nothing we've seen from him in Cleveland — either before he tore his Achilles in 2024 or during this preseason — that would make us think that Cleveland's offense is going to come alive. Plus, with defensive metrics that went from great to terrible depending on whether Myles Garrett was on the field, with the 2025 Defensive Player of the Year in Los Angeles, there's less to worry about for Trevor Lawrence. 

Estimated Availability: 100%

What you're giving up (projected point spread):

  • Week 10 at Titans (JAX -4.5)

  • Week 12 vs. Titans (JAX -7.5)

It can be a fool's errand to try to project who the easiest matchups will be down the road, when we haven't seen anyone play in the regular season, but the Jaguars do have a pair of games with the Titans — a team that's seen money come against them in Week 1 at home … against the New York Jets. 

Chargers (80.9%) over Cardinals 

For the second spot on this list — generally reserved for a significant favorite — the game with the biggest line (and likely to be the most popular pick) does come with some trepidation. 

Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett looked more capable last season than, say, Watson has. With legitimate weapons like Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr., the emergent Michael Wilson and a pair of new running backs, combined with some uncertainty around the Chargers breaking in a new defensive coordinator — and a new offensive coordinator — and you could envision more of a sweat than you thought you were bargaining for. 

Estimated Availability: 100%

What you're giving up (projected point spread):

  • Week 2 vs. Raiders (LAC -8.5)

  • Week 11 vs. Jets (LAC -8)

  • Week 16 at Dolphins (LAC -7.5)

The other reason(s) not to just roll with the chalk are that there are three other spots where the Chargers look appealing, and one is literally next week. 

At the moment, based on lookahead lines, there are two games with bigger betting lines in Week 2, and two nice options for later in the season might be enough for you to save the Chargers. 

Steelers (62.5%) over Falcons 

That the Steelers aren't even considered our "dark horse" pick only tells you how weird things might get for those either brave enough, or who are in a super-deep pool — where it's a necessity to zig while others zag. 

From a matchup perspective, if you're ever going to back a 42-year-old quarterback, doing so when the weather is warm is the time to do it. 

Aaron Rodgers' availability isn't the only consideration on the Pittsburgh side of things. For how long the defending AFC North champions will have a fully healthy defense is anyone's guess. Specifically, T.J. Watt, with whom the Steelers have a considerably better record than without, but also 37-year-old Cameron Hayward and a secondary featuring 31-year-old Jalen Ramsey and 29-year-old Jamel Dean (both older by defensive back standards). 

On the Falcons' side, Tua Tagovailoa will start Week 1, having done very little in the lead-up to the season to take the starting job from Michael Penix Jr., even as Penix Jr. recovers from ACL surgery. 

Rodgers is vulnerable against a formidable pass rush, but the Falcons are without both of 2025's highly-drafted edge rushers: Jalon Walker (season-ending injury) and James Pearce (eight-game suspension). 

Estimated Availability: 100%

What you're giving up (projected point spread):

  • Week 8 vs. Browns (PIT -3)

  • Week 17 at Titans (PIT -1.5)

Before you think we're irrationally high on the Steelers this season, the fact that the other two weeks where we might consider them come with spread projections shorter than this game with the Falcons should confirm that it might be now or never for Pittsburgh. 

You'll note that the Steelers didn't make our top-18 list above, but:

  1. Pittsburgh just missed the cut, as they're bunched with the Buccaneers and Commanders around the top 20

  2. So, if you're in a contest that requires more than 18 teams selected to get to the end (like, Circa's), then the Steelers become more viable 

  3. Once you get to the top 16-24 teams in power-ranking, the order becomes personal preference

The dark horse: Raiders (61.9%) over Dolphins

There's no darker horse than the Raiders, but if you're looking for a pick with a low selection percentage, you could do worse than backing a team actively trying to win this season versus one that's more "wait-and-see."

Kirk Cousins, healthy and with his old offensive coach from when they were both with the Vikings, provides more certainty on the offensive side than the Dolphins have with new quarterback Malik Willis, who doesn't have the same roster support around him that he had in Green Bay. 

While both teams have new regimes, the Raiders are further along in their rebuilding plan. For at least one game, Las Vegas has the ideal combination of already having its potential quarterback of the future, without dealing with the growing pains of starting Fernando Mendoza just yet.

Estimated Availability: 100%

What you're giving up (projected point spread):

  • Week 16 vs. Titans (LV -1)

I think you already knew there wasn't going to be another glaring spot to take the Raiders, but at least they might be favored at home against the Titans in Week 16? 

That's not something you'd want to plan for, though, as the Raiders aren't in anyone's top-18, 20, or even 25 teams, by power rating, and will likely have turned the team over to Mendoza by then.

So, maybe, if there's 20,000 other entries in your pool, finding yourself in a virtual "Black Hole," might be the way to play Week 1.

You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor Matt Russell at THE WINDOW.

item.title: Week 1 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets, including a play in Cowboys-Giants
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 1 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 1 of the NFL began with a 13-10 Seattle Seahawks win over the New England Patriots and continued on Thursday night with the NFL's first-ever regular season game played in Australia — a 27-7 victory by the San Francisco 49ers over the Los Angeles Rams.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Corbie Craig, Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 1 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5, 50.5)

Jacob: The highest total on the Week 1 NFL slate comes from Cincinnati — and it makes complete sense. After all, the Bengals' defense leaked like a broken water main all last season, while Tampa Bay's stop unit was well below average. Also, the two quarterbacks in this contest — Baker Mayfield and Joe Burrow — are big-armed veterans who combined for 43 touchdown passes in just 25 games in 2025.

Here's what you may not know: Burrow is a notorious slow starter. He has one total touchdown pass in the last three season openers. And for his career, he has many interceptions (five) as TD throws in Week 1. 

Now check out Cincinnati's points production in its six openers this decade: 17 (vs. Cleveland last year); 10 (vs. New England in 2024); 3 (at Cleveland in 2023); 20 (vs. Pittsburgh in overtime in 2022); 27 (vs. Minnesota in overtime in 2021); 13 (vs. the Chargers in 2020). Only the game against the Vikings (27-24 final) hurdled 43 combined points. 

To be fair, Mayfield has been spectacular in his three openers with Tampa Bay (nine TDs, zero INTs). However, only one of the Buccaneers' last four Week 1 games has cleared 43 points.

Then there's this: Since 2022, seven Week 1 contests have closed with a total of at least 50 points. Only twice did the over cash.

Bet: Under 50.5

Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings (-1.5, 46.5)

Jacob: Minnesota followed up its stunning 14-3 record in 2024 with a miserable start to last season, dropping eight of the first dozen games. Rather than throw in the towel, though, the Vikings regrouped and closed on a five-game winning streak to finish one game above .500. And they did it with J.J. McCarthy — now the team's third-string QB — starting four of the five contests.

Meanwhile, the 2025 Packers went the complete opposite direction, dropping their final four games after a 9-3-1 start to miss the playoffs for just the second time in seven years.

Bet the Minnesota Vikings to cover the spread at sportsbooks

Obviously, there's no certainty that late-season momentum — either positive or negative — will carry over to this year. But at least the Vikings' roster is in better shape: Minnesota enters the season without a single starter on the injured list. Conversely, Green Bay won't have ineligible running back Josh Jacobs (whose backups are completely unproven); three starting offensive lineman are banged up (and that unit lost two of last year's starters to free agency); star pass-rusher Micah Parsons (torn Achilles) is on IR; and two starting defensive linemen are questionable.

What about new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray? I believe he'll be a huge upgrade over McCarthy — in large part because I expect head coach Kevin O'Connell to resurrect Murray in the same way he did Sam Darnold two years ago.

Bet: Vikings -1.5 

Pond: We are about to experience the Justin Jefferson bounce-back season and it starts against the Packers in this NFC North showdown. 

The two-time, First-team All-Pro wide receiver is coming off a campaign he'd surely like to forget. Jefferson finished with career lows in yards (1,048), average yards per catch (12.5) and touchdowns (two) for a Minnesota team that went 9-8 and missed the playoffs.

A season removed from that disappointment, Jefferson will get things cooking with Murray under center against a Green Bay defense missing Parsons.

Jump on this ladder play featuring four wagers, and which includes three at plus money. You can tack on over 110 yards (+310) if you're looking to go even deeper on these bets.

Bet: Jefferson alt receiving yards — 70+ Yards (-136) | 80+ Yards (+110) | 90+ Yards (+158) | 100+ Yards (+225) at FanDuel

Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs (-2.5, 43.5)

Craig: KennethWalker III is walking into a crowded room in a new offense, in September, with a quarterback who has never handed him the ball in a game that counted. He ran for 1,027 yards on 221 carries across all 17 games for Seattle last season, which comes out to 60.4 yards a game, and the market has posted 61.5. That is last year's rate copied forward with a rounding error on top, and last year Walker was splitting a backfield in Seattle. He is not doing that now.

Kansas City signed him on March 12 to a three-year deal worth up to $45 million with $28.7 million guaranteed, and the Chiefs signed him to replace both Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt. You don't pay a running back like that to hand him the same workload he had somewhere else.

Our projection lands at 67.9 yards and the case is volume rather than efficiency. A back getting 13 carries a game in a duo now should be getting more than that as the highest-paid piece of a Kansas City backfield that has lost its two most-used players.

Bet: Kenneth Walker III over 61.5 rushing yards (-109)

Buffalo Bills (-1.5, 44.5) at Houston Texans

Craig: James Cook carried the ball 309 times in the regular season last year (18.2 attempts per game). He has been one of the most durable high-volume backs in football, and the market has him at 17.5 carries, which is a perfectly reasonable place to put a number for a back nobody has any reason to doubt. The problem with copying that number forward is that the man who called those plays is now the man running the team.

Offensive coordinator Joe Brady was promoted to head coach on Jan. 27 after Sean McDermott was fired, and Brady has already said publicly that Cook's workload was high and that the backfield needs to share it, with Ray Davis lined up behind him. That is not a beat writer's speculation — it's the head coach describing his own plan.

Then look at the opponent, because Houston fielded the best defense in football last season and then spent the whole offseason making the front even harder to run at, signing Logan Hall in free agency and trading up in the second round for Ohio State defensive tackle Kayden McDonald.

The last time these two teams played, Cook broke a 45-yard touchdown in the first quarter and then spent the rest of the afternoon grinding out 71 yards on his other 16 carries in a 23-19 Houston win, finishing with 17 attempts, which is under the number the market is asking you to lay today.

Bet: Cook under 17.5 rush attempts (-111)

Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5, 41.5)

Russell: It's Week 1, and we've already seen a star quarterback not make it out of the first series of the game, but the Falcons' quarterback situation looks to have that beat. Here are Atlanta's options to start at QB for a road game on Sunday:

  1. Michael Penix — not ready to return from an ACL injury.

  2. Tua Tagovailoa — already rumored to be on the chopping block barring epic performance, tumbled to the ground with a back issue in Thursday's practice.

  3. Cooper Rush — four interceptions, no touchdowns on 52 attempts last season.

  4. Jack Strand — undrafted free agent from Division II, Minnesota State-Moorhead.

Not to sound overly dramatic, but if the Steelers can't win this game by a touchdown or more, they should be eliminated from playoff contention. 

The Falcons come into the season rated in the market as a below-average team (40 out of 100 in THE WINDOW's estimated market ratings), but teams with quarterback debacles often see their rating for that week fall into the 20s. That would equate to a new line of Steelers -7, at least. 

Bet: Steelers -4.5

Dallas Cowboys (-3, 48.5) at New York Giants

Pond: I'm expecting fireworks in this matchup of NFC East rivals who will shine on offense and struggle mightily on defense.

Dallas averaged 27.7 points per game a season ago, finishing second in total offense (6,663 yards) and seventh in points. In contrast, the Cowboys were downright atrocious on defense. They conceded a league-worst 30.1 PPG and wound up third in yards allowed (6,409) during a 7-9-1 campaign.

As for the Giants, they weren't much better on the defensive front. They finished 26th in team defense and yielded the fifth-worst yards (6,112) overall a season ago.

Sure, both franchises are optimistic they'll be able to turn things around, but I'm not buying it. These are teams that will be hard to stop when they have the ball and poor trying to defend.

Dallas and New York combined for a whopping 77 points in Week 2 of the 2025 campaign and 51 points in the rematch. I don't think we hit that gaudy number here, but clearing this total shouldn't be an issue.

Bet: Over 47.5 (-128 at DraftKings)

Week 1 of the NFL season is already underway, and it's time to get those bets in for the weekend's matchups.

Action report from the bookmakers

Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans

Thomas Gable, sportsbook director at Borgata in Atlantic City: "Favorite has bounced back and forth here throughout the summer. Right now, the Bills are a small favorite, we have them a -1.5. This game has been pick-em, Texans -1, Bills -1 at one point. Decent percentage of the money is on the Bills. There's been a lot of public money on Buffalo here."

Joey Feazel, head NFL trader at Caesars Sportsbook: "Throughout the offseason, this has been back and forth. We opened up Bills -1.5, it had gone through the zero to Texans -1.5 at one point, and now back to Bills -1.5. I expect come game day with people remembering how bad CJ Stroud looked in the playoffs that we'll need the Texans. Still good two-way action right now."

Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers

Gable: "Bears currently laying 3. Not a ton of interest on this game here compared to other games on the board, but what we have taken has been mostly Bears money. Total is 47, pretty evenly split."

Bet Chicago Bears to cover the spread at sportsbooks right now

Feazel: "Another one where the offseason betting was high on Caleb Williams and the Bears. Not a lot of love for the Panthers despite making the playoffs and giving the Rams a run for their money. Little bit more on the Bears side. We opened this Bears -2.5, we're now at Chicago -3 and it's a heavy 3. Total has gone up a couple points. It opened 44.5, now up to 46.5. We're not crazy lopsided."

Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings

Gable: "Vikings are a 1.5-point favorite. This game is relatively split. The public has come in a bit on Green Bay, but overall a pretty evenly bet game. Total is 46.5, no decision on that one yet. We did have some respected money on the Vikings in the summer when Packers were favored."

Feazel: "This is one that has moved the most out of any Week 1 game. We opened Packers -2.5, and slowly but surely it's trickled to Vikings -1.5. I think it's a couple things — no Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs not playing and excitement for Kyler Murray being installed into the system. The J.J. McCathy experiment didn't go to plan last year. Total has gone up a point from 45.5 to 46.5. I don't anticipate that much to change there. Not super one-sided on the Vikings, but a little more money on Minnesota so far. In the latter half of last year, public was soured by Green Bay and shied away from this team covering. I expect to see two-way action and I don't see this going back to the Packers being favored."

Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants

Gable: "This game has the most handle of any game on the board. Cowboys are sitting -3. Dallas has been the darling of the betting world. Their futures have moved significantly — division, season win total, you name it. We are getting Giants money here, some local money. As of right now, we'll need Dallas, which I don't hate, but this game is generating a lot of betting interest."

Feazel: "No surprise here, the Cowboys are taking the majority of action and I expect that to continue. What people remember from Dallas is how efficient that offense was. We're going to see over and Cowboys-centric money. We opened 49, down to 47.5, but I expect that to come back up by game day."

Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs

Gable: "As expected, if Chiefs are -3 you're taking Broncos money and at -2.5, taking Chiefs money. Currently, KC is -2.5, which it has been for a week or so. Total at 43.5, no real decision on that. It's one of those games where it's been bouncing back and forth. We have a little bit more money on the Chiefs."

Feazel: "Not a lot of love for the Chiefs at all here. A lot of question markets around Mahomes, defense gets a little worse. More action on the Broncos side, which isn't something we're accustomed to — but not surprising after the Chiefs' struggles. Total opened 44, down to 43.5. I expect one-way action on Denver leading up to the game. We opened -3, now a strong -2.5. I don't anticipate it getting back to -3."

Sharp action

It's always notable where respected bettors have landed on this week's games. While these prices may not currently be available at all sportsbooks, knowing where sharps have wagered can also be instructive for in-game wagering.

Yahoo Sports conversed with several bookmakers this preseason and over the course of this week, and here is where some sharp action has been (and the numbers it came in at):

  • Bengals -3, Bucs +4

  • Dolphins +3.5

  • Colts +3.5

  • Steelers -3, -3.5

  • Lions-Saints over 48.5

  • Cardinals +10

item.title: 5 Bold Predictions for Ravens at Colts Regular Season Opener
item.description: 5 bold predictions for the Colts regular season opener against the Ravens!
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts kick off their regular season at home against the Baltimore Ravens this afternoon, and here are five bold predictions ahead of today’s matchup:

1. Sauce Gardner locks down Zay Flowers early
Flowers is dealing with a hamstring issue and drew a hefty target share expectation, but he’ll be seeing plenty of Sauce Gardner in man coverage. If Gardner wins that matchup in the first half, it takes away Baltimore’s easiest answer when the offensive line struggles — and that line is the year’s biggest question mark for the Ravens.

2. Colts RB Jonathan Taylor exploits Ravens head coach Jesse Minter’s defense again
Taylor torched Minter’s Los Angeles Chargers defense for 94 total rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns last October, as head coach Jim Harbaugh’s former defensive coordinator. Minter’s scheme hasn’t fundamentally changed, and the Ravens are breaking in new pass rushers up front (with starting Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike out). Expect Taylor to be the tone-setter often that keeps Indy’s offense ahead of schedule, especially with starting quarterback Daniel Jones working his way back from a torn Achilles early on.

3. The Colts win the pressure battle without blitzing much
Minter’s defenses have historically blitzed at a low rate (19% last year), which means the Colts’ front — led by DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart — gets to win with four rushers against a Ravens line PFF ranks 24th in the league, including a center making his first career start. Clean pocket push, not exotic pressure packages, is how Indy and Colts veteran defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo gets to Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson.

4. Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones avoids the big mistake
Jones enters surprisingly healthy after last year’s late Achilles injury, and Indy’s offense was historically explosive by EPA/play under Colts head coach Shane Steichen. If he protects the ball against a Baltimore defense that’s also breaking in new pieces, field position swings the Colts’ way in a game expected to be low-scoring and close.

5. Colts win a tight one at home, something like 24-20
Baltimore is favored by 3.5 with a 47.5 total, but a lot of that leans on unknowns — new OC Declan Doyle calling his first regular-season game, a shaky interior line, and Jackson playing behind a center with zero career starts. The Colts faithful’s rapid noise, plus a battle-tested Colts offensive identity tips a close one to Indianapolis.

item.title: Rams suggested as landing spot for reunion with former tackle
item.description: Should Rams sign D.J. Humphries again?
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders released tackle D.J. Humphries on Friday, opening the door for him to return to the Los Angeles Rams as insurance for A.J. Jackson if that’s something both parties are interested in. Humphries appeared in eight games with the Rams in 2025, including one start in place of Jackson. It is also possible that the Commanders are simply releasing Humphries for roster considerations with the expectation to re-sign him in Week 2, but in any case the Rams do have the opportunity to sign the veteran tackle if they want.

Josh Buckhalter of Heavy suggested the Rams should reach out to Humphries in case Jackson is suspended or loses time due to injury again:

Humphries also has one start in four postseason appearances and has a pre-existing relationship with Rams assistant head coach Kliff Kingsbury.

“The offense is kind of–it’s kind of the offense that I ran earlier with Kliff and, I guess, a lot of that same stuff,” Humphries told reporters in August, underscoring how much of an impact the first-year Rams coach had on him (and the Commanders).

“It’s easier for me to kind of mesh in. “

Humphries was the 24th overall pick in the 2015 draft by the Arizona Cardinals. He started 98 games with the Cardinals over eight seasons and has since signed with the Chiefs, Rams, and Commanders. He has been firmly entrenched as a backup over the past two years.

Jackson has not been suspended by the NFL yet and may not be suspended at all. However, L.A. only has one backup left tackle right now and it’s 36-year-old journeyman David Quessenberry. With Humphries now a free agent again, perhaps Les Snead would feel more comfortable with him coming back to the Rams.
